decisions.reason: The candidate already records the connector-placement clauses from message 842. The antenna direction and keepout remain an independently represented RF-layout requirement and do not alter the candidate's existing attributes.
Applying the antenna constraint to the integrated-board variant does not change the selected board architectures, their roles, or the integrated variant's functionality and design goal.
The antenna direction and PCB keepout do not explicitly change the enclosure's accommodations, mounts, airflow, assembly, or retention requirements.

This candidate governs connector placement for the three-board variant, while the source change extends an antenna constraint to the integrated-board variant without changing the separate-board connector rules.
Antenna orientation and keepout do not change the required pin coverage, through-hole breakout format, hole-placement flexibility, or platform purpose.
The source concerns the integrated board's ESP32 antenna and does not modify the separate power board's dimensions, orientation, mounting holes, or connector placement.
The antenna keepout is an additional RF-layout constraint but does not explicitly change the candidate's board dimensions, adjustability, or general routing-space acceptance condition.
The ESP32 antenna constraint does not affect the sensor board's requirement to fit its required components and connectors.
The integrated-board antenna direction and keepout do not change the power board's four-layer stack requirement.
The source imposes a physical antenna-layout constraint and does not modify any component sourcing, availability, cost, or JLCPCB classification policy.
Antenna orientation and keepout do not change the requirement to use through-hole connector mounting technology.
The antenna constraint does not alter the three-board interboard power topology, connector specifications, pin-order rule, or sensor-board power input.
